title: Global poverty reduction is stalling because public buffers remain uneven across life stage, work status, place, and fiscal scale
source_unit: United Nations Statistics Division and UN DESA, SDG Indicators 2026, Goal 1: No Poverty
geography: Global; country and regional comparisons across poverty, social protection, public spending, working poverty, and development assistance

denominator.unit: global population at the $3.00/day 2021 PPP threshold

extreme_poverty_rate.unit: percent of global population estimated to live in extreme poverty in 2026

extreme_poor_count.unit: million people estimated to live in extreme poverty in 2026

2030_projection.unit: percent of global population projected to remain in extreme poverty in 2030

concentration.value: 71% of the world’s extreme poor are concentrated in sub-Saharan Africa

mechanism.value: A slowing global average can coexist with persistent regional poverty traps where conflict, climate shocks, weak opportunity, and thin protection compound

observations.method: UN SDG indicator estimates and projections using the $3.00/day 2021 PPP extreme-poverty threshold and regional aggregation.
observations.uncertainty: Global poverty estimates depend on survey coverage, purchasing-power revisions, projections, and regional aggregation; they do not measure multidimensional deprivation or household trajectories.
observations.subgroup: People in sub-Saharan Africa, fragile and conflict-affected settings, rural areas, and households exposed to climate and cost shocks.
observations.counterinterpretation: Aggregate poverty reduction can accelerate if growth, transfers, peace, and measurement improve; the projection is not a fixed forecast.

observations.period: 2023; global social-protection coverage by population group

denominator.unit: global population and population groups covered by at least one social-protection benefit

any_benefit_coverage.unit: percent of global population covered by at least one social-protection benefit

unprotected_population.unit: billion people without any form of social protection

old_age_coverage.unit: percent of people above retirement age covered by old-age pensions

unemployment_coverage.unit: percent of unemployed persons covered by unemployment protection

mechanism.value: The same shock is buffered very differently depending on whether a person is old, unemployed, a child, a new mother, disabled, or in a covered labor market

observations.method: UN SDG indicator compilation of social-protection coverage across population groups and benefit types.
observations.uncertainty: Coverage means receipt or legal coverage of at least one benefit and does not establish adequacy, access quality, duration, or protection against poverty.
observations.subgroup: Children, mothers with newborns, persons with severe disabilities, workers, unemployed people, and older persons.
observations.counterinterpretation: Coverage can be a meaningful first-stage capability even where benefit adequacy or service quality remains unmeasured.

observations.period: 2023; public social spending reaching the poorest 20 percent

denominator.unit: countries or areas with comparable data for at least one sector; 54 cover education, health, and transfers

combined_bottom_quintile_share.unit: average percent of combined education, health, and direct-transfer spending reaching the poorest 20 percent

direct_transfer_share.unit: average percent of direct cash and near-cash transfers reaching the poorest 20 percent

health_share.unit: average percent of health spending reaching the poorest 20 percent

mechanism.value: Public spending is not automatically pro-poor; the delivery channel and institutional design determine how much aggregate spending becomes reachable household support

observations.method: UN analysis of comparable public-spending incidence data for education, health, and direct transfers.
observations.uncertainty: Country comparability is limited by data availability and incidence methods; average shares do not show benefit adequacy, administrative exclusion, or within-country distribution.
observations.subgroup: The poorest 20 percent, households using public health and education systems, and recipients of cash or near-cash transfers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Universal services may generate broad benefits not captured by bottom-quintile incidence alone, including prevention, social mobility, and risk pooling.

denominator.unit: global employed population and official development assistance grants targeting poverty reduction

working_poverty.unit: million workers living in extreme poverty in 2025

working_poverty_rate.unit: percent of employed population living in extreme poverty in 2025

oda_decline.unit: percent decline in poverty-reduction ODA grants between 2023 and 2024

poverty_reduction_oda.unit: billion dollars in poverty-reduction ODA grants in 2024

health_aid_drop.unit: billion-dollar decline in basic health aid between 2023 and 2024

mechanism.value: Work does not guarantee security, and shrinking external finance can weaken the public buffers needed to convert employment and services into durable poverty reduction

observations.method: UN SDG analysis of working-poverty indicators and OECD/official development-assistance grant data.
observations.uncertainty: Working-poverty and aid figures are aggregate measures; they do not identify household-level receipt, aid effectiveness, or causal effects of funding changes.
observations.subgroup: Young workers, workers in sub-Saharan Africa and least-developed countries, aid-dependent communities, and households relying on health, food, education, or social infrastructure grants.
observations.counterinterpretation: Domestic revenue, remittances, private provision, and improved aid allocation may offset some external-funding decline, though these channels are not measured here.

related_sources.claim: Official extended 2026 SDG report and indicator context.
UN SDG indicator framework and global reporting portal.

boundary: This record adds a global household-security route from poverty and work through social-protection coverage, benefit-type inequality, public-spending incidence, aid retrenchment, and state buffering. It is an official SDG indicator synthesis using aggregate estimates and projections, not respondent-level longitudinal evidence, a causal evaluation of transfers, or a direct measure of household welfare adequacy.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official UN SDG Goal 1 page was reviewed for extreme poverty, social-protection coverage, public-spending incidence, working poverty, and poverty-reduction aid findings.
